body:
## Problem

The complexity, duplication and performance audit of #637 identified probe costs that become significant with many stations, many accepted tracking substeps, or large particle counts. This issue tracks the deliberately deferred work after cyclotron/FFA crossing and old-OPAL parity validation.

The audited revision is [`b1551b9c337c0c57dd21a4e2e26ccaff10fdfc93`](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/commit/b1551b9c337c0c57dd21a4e2e26ccaff10fdfc93). The costs below are established from source inspection and local compile-time layout checks. Actual wall-clock slowdowns and achievable speedups have not been measured; the existing one-particle A100 comparisons establish correctness, not production throughput.

Audit items 2, 5 and 6—accelerating-PIC failure-record storage, duplicate sector support evaluation and RF validation/setup cleanup—are being handled separately from this issue. This issue should remain open independently of merging #637. General out-of-field-map shutdown remains covered by #672.

## Observed costs

### 1. One global error reduction per station per accepted endpoint

[`CyclotronProbeRecorder::observe`](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/b1551b9c337c0c57dd21a4e2e26ccaff10fdfc93/src/Algorithms/CyclotronProbeRecorder.cpp#L130) loops over stations. Each iteration resets a device counter, launches a device reduction with a host result, performs `MPI_Allreduce`, transfers the hit count and creates/copies a compact host hit mirror. No-hit steps and ranks with no local particles still participate.

Sixteen stations therefore introduce sixteen global error reductions for each observed accepted endpoint, plus GPU synchronization/transfer overhead. A 36,245-step run incurs approximately 580,000 such reductions per active container, excluding initialization and segment refresh. The refresh before an integration segment is once per segment, not an additional observation every step.

Candidate work: batch station validity flags into one collective per observation, then batch compact counts/transfers and consider a station-aware kernel organization. Preserve collective error propagation and avoid letting one rank advance while another reports invalid data.

### 2. Repeated endpoint history increases storage and migration payload

[`cyclotron_probe::State`](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/b1551b9c337c0c57dd21a4e2e26ccaff10fdfc93/src/Algorithms/CyclotronProbe.h#L36) contains two directed observer states, each carrying the previous accepted position, momentum and time. The same endpoint is also repeated across every station. Every station history is a registered IPPL particle attribute and travels with particle sorting, compaction and MPI migration.

The audited local ABI sizes are: endpoint 56 bytes, directed state 72 bytes, station history 160 bytes and compact hit 96 bytes. Thus sixteen stations add 2,560 bytes of history per allocated particle:

| Particles | History for sixteen stations |
|---:|---:|
| 4,096 | 10 MiB |
| 32,768 | 80 MiB |
| 262,144 | 640 MiB |
| 1,000,000 | 2.38 GiB |

These values exclude spare capacity, other particle attributes, output and MPI buffers. The compact hit scratch buffer is shared between stations and costs 96 bytes per local high-water particle count; it must not be multiplied by the station count.

Candidate work: retain one migratable previous laboratory endpoint per particle and compact station-specific arming/passage state. Preserve stable-ID association and the out-of-line history allocation/initialization/deletion boundary required by shared-library CUDA builds.

### 3. Cyclotron summary flushing scales with accumulated turns

The recorder flushes every 100 accepted global steps. Its [cumulative summary loop](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/b1551b9c337c0c57dd21a4e2e26ccaff10fdfc93/src/Algorithms/CyclotronProbeRecorder.cpp#L183) reduces the full histogram and performs a separate `MPI_Reduce` for each historical turn before replacing `.hist` and `.peaks`. It performs that work even when the phase-space sink has no new hits. A maximum observed reference-turn label of 200 means 201 small peak reductions per station per flush.

Candidate work: pack per-turn sums/counts into one array reduction and use globally agreed dirty state to skip unchanged summary rewrites. Retain cumulative output and flush-on-failure behavior. FFA already disables lab-origin radial summaries and must continue producing only its native phase-space records.

## Additional follow-ups

- Cache immutable sector/gap classification and ordered occurrences during preparation. [`hasCyclotronGaps` and reference gap assembly](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/b1551b9c337c0c57dd21a4e2e26ccaff10fdfc93/src/Algorithms/ParallelTracker.cpp#L1108) repeatedly inspect the lattice, and `OpalBeamline::getElements()` reconstructs a set by value. This debt predates #637; the extension increases its use. Preserve occurrence ordering and placement semantics.
- Bound general adapter memory for large station files. [`probe_frame_adapter.py`](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/b1551b9c337c0c57dd21a4e2e26ccaff10fdfc93/tools/probe_frame_adapter.py#L66) currently retains HDF5 batches, concatenates and globally sorts them, then validates/copies DataFrames repeatedly. Ten 64-bit columns alone require 800 MB for ten million records, before copies, sorting and Python integer lists. Consider efficient validation of already typed arrays and an explicit batch-ordered export mode. Streaming must not silently replace documented global bunch/ID/time ordering.

Root-gathered ASCII output with per-record flushing and HDF5 batch-statistics work in `LossDataSink` are inherited writer costs. Profile them separately; do not attribute their implementation to this PR or broaden this task into an unconditional writer rewrite.

## Staged work and acceptance

- [ ] Establish reproducible OFF/ON baselines with fixed input/particle hashes and probes disabled or 1, 4 and 16 stations. Use representative particle counts, including at least 32,768 and 262,144 where resources permit; include many boundary substeps, no-hit intervals and empty local ranks.
- [ ] Record accepted step counts, wall time, peak device/host memory, probe kernel/host-transfer time, MPI collective counts/time, migration payload/time and output time. Record toolchain, CPU/GPU model, ranks and threads. Test single-rank and multi-rank runs, including CUDA on supported hardware. Report a workload matrix rather than inferring throughput from one-particle comparisons.
- [ ] Batch station error communication and compact transfers. Keep every accepted interval observable; reducing observation frequency can miss crossings and is not an acceptable optimization.
- [ ] Batch and avoid unchanged cyclotron summary work, retaining every-100-step and terminal/failure flush behavior.
- [ ] Redesign history storage only after baseline coverage and measurements are available. Verify allocation growth, sorting, deletion, MPI ownership changes and shared-library CUDA lifecycle behavior.
- [ ] Address lattice metadata caching and adapter memory as separate measured increments.

For each increment, verify probe ON/OFF physical particle and reference states, accepted timesteps, fields and stopping decisions. Retain bidirectional finite-segment crossings, interpolation/hysteresis and initial-plane suppression, stable IDs, multiple crossings per shared reference turn, native laboratory coordinates, step-start reference-turn labels, ASCII/HDF5 batch semantics, charge/mass and duplicate-free flushing. Test collectively raised failures without deadlock and preserve previously accepted diagnostic records.

Use exact comparisons on deterministic, otherwise identical configurations where already established. Document any change in floating-point reduction order and justify its numerical effect; do not relax existing tolerances simply to pass. Native unit tests must remain self-contained C++ with no external Python scripts, supplied datasets or launched OPALX processes. Keep benchmark/integration drivers separate.
title: Reduce probe synchronization, history storage and cumulative summary overhead
